classes: World (anonymous CrashReport Callables in getBiomeGenForCoords, func_147460_e, updateEntities and addWorldInfoToCrashReport)
role: The shared base of WorldServer and WorldClient: block get/set with neighbour notification, the light engine, entity and tile-entity lists and the per-tick entity pass, collision and material queries, raytrace and explosion helpers, weather and the day clock, the chunk tick's active set and mood sound, player lookups, and the World.rand and updateLCG streams everything else draws from.
scope_reason: Every server tick and every client frame goes through World. Redstone power reads are forced to 0 by world.conf redstone = off (hooked at isBlockProvidingPowerTo and getIndirectPowerLevelTo), which the native side mirrors.

notes: Read with comments stripped; members are complete to my reading of the file. Many helpers are re-implemented per file (isAirBlock, doesBlockHaveSolidTopSurface, getTopSolidOrLiquidBlock, getBlockLightValue); the member cites one representative. Oracle hooks in this file: Det.newRandom for rand and updateLCG, Rows.onAttempt/onBlock/onAttemptEnd in setBlock and setBlockMetadataWithNotify, Oracle.quietJoin in updateEntities, Oracle.calendar and calendarMillis for theCalendar and getCurrentDate, WorldConf.redstone at isBlockProvidingPowerTo and getIndirectPowerLevelTo. Status exact at member level means a named native port exists; I did not rerun recordings. Where a member cites a struct field (servertick.h total_time etc.) the logic is inline at its users. Closed by lane/idxworld: each partial or missing member was checked against the Java call sites and the native port (the member notes); a member used only by a switched-off feature or by no reachable caller is n/a with the reason. One player per environment is SPEC's scope (the single-player integrated server; LAN play is not in this game), so the player lists hold one.
